1.why: The system enforces server-side authorization on MFA endpoints by checking session.accountId against the account owner (accountForSession).

2.why: The same verification code cannot work for another user because the identityKey binds the code to a specific account (email+phone).

3.why: Previous sessions are invalidated when a new authenticated session is created (sessions.delete(pending.id) and sessions.set(authenticated.id, authenticated)).

4.why: OTP secrets and backup codes are stored encrypted (encryptSecret) or hashed (hashValue), not in plain text.

5.why: Secrets and codes are generated using cryptographically secure RNG (crypto.getRandomValues and secureInt).

6.why: Secrets, OTPs, and session tokens are not stored in browser storage or non-HttpOnly cookies (session cookies are HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict).

7.why: Server-side input (email, phone, OTP) is validated using regex and type checks (validEmail, validPhone, validOtp).

8.why: Values rendered in HTML are escaped by default (e.g., textContent in JavaScript, no innerHTML usage).

9.why: Redirects are not explicitly handled, but allowedPaths restricts navigation to internal URLs only.

10.why: Secure headers (CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options) are set in headersFor.

11.why: Session cookies are set with HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict attributes (cookieHeader).

12.why: OTP seeds, backup codes, and session tokens are not exposed in logs, URLs, or error output (genericError masks details).

13.why: Verification codes are single-use (identityUsed flag) and time-bound (identityExpiresAt).

14.why: Rate-limiting is enforced for failed verification attempts (identityFailures, identityLockUntil, VERIFICATION_FAILURE_THRESHOLD).

15.why: Session identifiers are rotated on authentication (rotateAuthenticatedSession), have idle/absolute timeouts, and are invalidated on logout (sessions.delete).
